scientific_question: Does the association between commuting and sleep time differ between men and women?
falsifiable_claim: The coefficient for sleep_weekday_min on commute_5h is more negative among females than among males.

observed_evidence.statement: Adjusted sleep_weekday_min coefficient = -48.711 (95% pointwise CI [-63.481, -33.94]; Bonferroni outcome interval [-67.565, -29.856])

scientific_inference.statement: Overall the association is negative, suggesting possible variation across subgroups such as sex.

unresolved_uncertainty: Whether the negative association is stronger for females than for males is unknown.

supporting_observation: the 95% interval of the difference (female minus male coefficient) excludes zero on the negative side
contradicting_observation: the 95% interval of the difference includes zero

engine_capability_assessment.reason: Testing a sex interaction requires interaction terms, which are not part of the current experiment specification
engine_capability_assessment.assessed_by: hypothesis_agent (provisional; the Experiment Planner decides feasibility)

limitations: Observational, cross‑sectional design; cannot infer causality.
Interaction test not pre‑specified; requires additional modeling not currently approved.

source_artifacts.integrity: content identical; LF checkout of CRLF-validated bytes

provenance.validation: contract, approved variables, observational language, numbers traceable to sources
